neighbours.label: biological aging and senescence: telomeres, age-related decline, lifespan (the + pole is the other end of life: embryos, development)
fire: Scientists study why telomere length declines as cells grow old and stop dividing.
The clinic sells anti-aging creams that promise to reverse the signs of getting older.
Senescent cells pile up in tissues and speed up age-related decline.
Caloric restriction slowed aging in rhesus monkeys and lengthened their lives.
A rare disease called progeria causes children to age prematurely.
Telomerase activity keeps the chromosome ends from wearing down in dividing cells.
Researchers hope a drug could delay the biological clock of ageing in older adults.
Longevity labs are testing whether young blood can rejuvenate old mice.
quiet: Scientists study how neurons carry signals as the brain learns a new task.
The clinic sells sunscreen creams that promise to prevent burns on hot days.
White blood cells pile up in tissues and fight off bacterial infection.
A high-fat diet raised cholesterol in rhesus monkeys and damaged their arteries.
A rare disease called hemophilia stops children's blood from clotting.
Ribosome activity turns messenger RNA into proteins in dividing cells.
The winery let the red wine age in oak for three years before bottling.
Embryo labs are testing how stem cells form the early heart in mice.

notes: Tests the meaning without one word: telomere, senescence, progeria, longevity. 'Aging' of wine is a near miss for the word without the meaning.
